 Ripple and Stellar outlook: What next as XRP returns to November 2024 levels and XLM touches a two-year low?
 By: Manish Chhetri , FXStreet Tags: XRP Updated: 17 Nov 2026 Make us preferred on Google 
 Selling pressure keeps XRP below $0.957 on Tuesday, following last week’s fall to its lowest level since mid-November 2024. 
 After Saturday’s slide to a two-year low of $0.130, XLM trades around $0.137. 
 Both altcoins remain vulnerable to further losses as on-chain metrics weaken and technical indicators deteriorate, even with oversold conditions. 
 Selling pressure continues to weigh on Ripple (XRP) and Stellar (XLM), with bears showing no sign of easing their grip. Tuesday’s weakness sees XRP return to November 2024 levels, while XLM touched a two-year low last week. Although both tokens have entered oversold territory, worsening on-chain metrics and bearish technical signals point to the risk of additional losses.
 TMGM Analysis: Financial Market News, Economic Calendar & Market Insights What do weaker on-chain metrics signal? 
 A bearish picture for both altcoins emerges from CryptoQuant’s summary data. In XRP’s spot and futures markets, large whale orders are evident, but sellers dominate. Both markets also display heating conditions, underscoring a broadly bearish and cautious mood among Ripple traders.
 Summary chart for XRP. Source: CryptoQuant Selling also dominates XLM’s spot and futures markets. Large whale sell orders appear in the spot market, while the remaining metrics are neutral. Taken together, these readings indicate a cautious-to-bearish stance among XLM traders.
 Summary chart for XLM. Source: CryptoQuant XRP technical outlook: Can XRP recover after revisiting November 2024 levels? 
 The near-term outlook for XRP remains bearish as its decline extends well below the 50-day, 100-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs), positioned at $1.217, $1.261 and $1.325, respectively. On Tuesday, the token trades at $0.955, having fallen to $0.893 on Saturday, a level last seen in mid-November 2024.
 At 25, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is in oversold territory, indicating that the downside move is stretched. However, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) continues to sit below zero. This points to persistent selling pressure, even as a corrective rebound remains possible.
 Any recovery would first encounter resistance at the psychological $1.000 mark, with the horizontal barrier at $1.160 next in line. Further up, the 100-day EMA at $1.261 and the $1.300 level create a broader ceiling. Beyond these sit the 200-day EMA at $1.325 and resistance at $1.540, marking the upper boundaries for any medium-term recovery attempt.
 Daily price chart for XRP/USDT XLM technical outlook: Can XLM turn around after hitting a two-year low? 
 A bearish near-term bias persists for XLM as the token extends its decline well below key EMAs. Following Saturday’s fall to a two-year low of $0.130, it trades at $0.137 on Tuesday. Momentum is still weak: the RSI is close to the oversold threshold at around 31, while the MACD remains below zero, with a slightly negative line and a muted histogram. These signals suggest sellers retain control, although the downward momentum is slowing.
 For an advance, the first resistance lies at the former horizontal barrier of $0.143. The previous trendline base near $0.153, which now acts as resistance after being breached, is the next obstacle. Higher up, a tight technical ceiling is formed by the 50-day EMA at $0.167 and horizontal resistance at $0.173, before the 100-day EMA at $0.175 and the 200-day EMA at $0.183.
 Only a daily close back above this cluster of averages would support a more substantial bullish reversal. The next major obstacle would then be horizontal resistance at $0.234, the upper boundary of the wider range.
